proofs.proof_tex:
Fix the displayed \(\rho\), dataset, and realized cell \(C\). Under the Fisher completion, every observed unit has the same known response under both candidate treatment labels. Hence, for every \((H'_{n,s},z'_{n1s})\in\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\), all summands defining \(X'_{n,s}\) are known. If a candidate arm count or variance is degenerate, the stated totalization \(X'_{n,s}=c_s-1\) is also known, so \(C'_n(\rho)\) is always imputable. The same completion makes every rank \(U'_{nksi}\), candidate contrast \(R'_{kj}\), and totalized value in its degenerate case known. For a retained stratum, a quota-respecting \(z'_{n2s}\) consequently determines \(R'_{2j}\) and \(T'_j\); for \(C_s=0\), chronology generates no stage--\(2\) coordinate.

By definition, \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\) imposes exactly four conditions: each holdout has size \(\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor\), each stage--\(1\) assignment has quota \(m_{n1s}\), the recomputed full signed label is \(C'_n(\rho)=C\), and each generated stage--\(2\) assignment in a retained stratum has quota \(m_{n2s}\). The preceding paragraph proves imputability on every history satisfying these conditions.

Conversely, a quota-respecting chronological history has its stage--\(1\) coordinate in \(\prod_s\Omega_{n,1s}(\rho)\). If its recomputed label is \(C\), it passes the sole restriction used in forming the same-cell fiber. Chronology then supplies, and only supplies, a quota-respecting stage--\(2\) vector for each \(s\) with \(C_s=1\). Thus it satisfies the defining conditions of \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)\). Since \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}>0\), normalization is defined. No further event is present in either implication.

At \(h=0\), no interference and the definition of \(Y^{(0)}\) give
\[
Y^{(0)}_{nksi}(1)=Y^{(0)}_{nksi}(0)=B_{nksi}\qquad(k\in K,\ s\in S,\ i\le N_{nks}).
\]
Consequently the Fisher completion equals the fixed baseline array on every observed coordinate, independently of the realized assignments. By the random-holdout and stage--\(1\) complete-randomization assumptions, a candidate stage--\(1\) history has the product mass displayed in \(\mathsf R^{0,\mathrm{base}}_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}\). By fixed thresholds, its selected label is exactly the deterministic recomputation \(C'_n(\rho)\). Conditional on \(C'_n(\rho)=C\), the stage--\(2\) assumption gives the independent product of uniform quota-respecting laws only for \(s\) with \(C_s=1\). The explicit-support lemma shows that the resulting support is precisely \(\Omega_{n,C}(\mathcal D_n^{0,\rho},\rho)\). Bayes' formula therefore gives, for every supported history \(\omega\),
\[
\mathsf P_n^{0,\rho}\{\omega\mid E_{n,C}(\rho)\}
=\frac{1}{p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,C,\mathcal D_n^{0,\rho},\rho)}
\prod_{s\in S}\!\left\{\binom{N_{n1s}}{\lfloor\rho N_{n1s}\rfloor}\binom{N_{n1s}}{m_{n1s}}\right\}^{-1}
\prod_{s:C_s=1}\binom{N_{n2s}}{m_{n2s}}^{-1},
\]
which is exactly \(\mathsf R^{0,C}_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}\{\omega\}\).

For completeness, on any finite probability space with statistic \(T\), define the nonrandomized upper-tail value \(p(T)=P\{T'\ge T\}\), where \(T'\) has that same law. If its distinct values are \(t_1>\cdots>t_L\) with masses \(w_l\), then \(p(t_l)=\sum_{a\le l}w_a\), and hence
\[
P\{p(T)\le u\}=\sum_{l:\,\sum_{a\le l}w_a\le u}w_l\le u,\qquad 0\le u\le1.
\]
Thus ties only make the value conservative. Applying this inequality to the conditional law just identified proves conditional superuniformity. Equivalently, if \(q=\inf\{x:F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(x)\ge1-\alpha\}\), then \(P\{T_j>q\mid E_{n,C}(\rho)\}\le\alpha\). Averaging the displayed conditional inequality over any ancillary realized information preserves it, so the test has finite-sample conditional level at most \(\alpha\).

For each stratum \(t\), let \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) denote its holdout and stage--\(1\) assignment history. The random-holdout and stage--\(1\) design assumptions give independence of \((\mathcal H_{nt})_{t\in S}\). Moreover \(X_{n,t}\) and the event \(\{X_{n,t}>c_t\}\) are measurable functions of \(\mathcal H_{nt}\) and its fixed potential outcomes. Conditional on the combined stage--\(1\) history, the stage--\(2\) assumption supplies mutually independent stratum-local kernels. We may equivalently pre-generate these kernels and reveal only those in recruited strata. Thus, for \(j=(C,s)\) and measurable \(B_0\), independence gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,E_{n,C}(\rho)\}\\
&\quad=\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\in B_0,X_{n,s}>c_s\}
\prod_{t\ne s}p_{nt}^{C_t}(1-p_{nt})^{1-C_t}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The same calculation with \(B_0\) equal to the whole space gives the cell probability. The sampling-selection margin makes its denominator positive eventually, and division cancels every factor indexed by \(t\ne s\).

Under \(\mathsf R^{0,\mathrm{base}}_{n,\mathcal D(\rho)}\), the candidate mass is a product over \(t\), and the completed outcomes and maps \(X'_{n,t}\) are stratum-local. Hence the signed stage--\(1\) cell probability factors as \(\prod_t(p'_{nt})^{C_t}(1-p'_{nt})^{1-C_t}\). Restriction to \(C'_n=C\) divides by this product, and the subsequently generated stage--\(2\) reference law is again a product over retained strata. The positivity premise on \(p_{\mathrm{ref}}\) permits this division. The identical argument applies to the independent Gaussian stage--\(1\) blocks and independent stage--\(2\) coordinates in the Gaussian experiment.

For the active coordinate, write \(X_s=a_j(\rho)h_s+Z\) and
\[
T_j=d_j(\theta_j)h_s+r_j(\rho,\theta_j)Z+v_j(\rho,\theta_j)E,
\]
where \(Z,E\) are independent standard normals. Under the null, conditioning on \(X_s>c_s\) is conditioning on \(Z>c_s\), so the upper-tail equation at level \(\alpha\) is exactly the displayed definition of \(q_{\alpha,j}\). Under the local alternative it is conditioning on \(Z>c_s-a_j(\rho)h_s\); integrating first over \(E\) gives exactly the displayed formula for \(\Pi_j\). This proves both the product cancellation and the scalar formulas without dropping any negative inequality in the complete cell.

Fix a block and suppress \((n,k,s)\). From \(\max_i x_i^4\le\sum_i x_i^4\), the fourth-moment assumption gives
\[
\max_i(B_i-\bar B)^2\le\left\{\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^4\right\}^{1/2}\le\sqrt{M_4N}.
\]
The variance margin gives \(\sum_i(B_i-\bar B)^2=(N-1)S_B^2\ge(N-1)\epsilon\). Division proves the first displayed inequality. Positive shares imply \(N_{nks}\to\infty\) uniformly over the finite set \(K\times S\), so its right side tends to zero.

For normalized midranks, \(0\le U_i^0\le1\), whence \(\max_i(U_i^0-\bar U^0)^2\le1\). Again the variance margin yields \(\sum_i(U_i^0-\bar U^0)^2\ge(N-1)\epsilon\), proving the second inequality and its limit. Every division uses \(\epsilon>0\), and uniformity follows because \(K\times S\) is finite and all limiting shares are positive.

By the definition of \(\kappa_j\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives \(|\kappa_j|\le1\). Since \(\rho\in[\rho_0,1-\rho_0]\) and \(0\le\cos^2\theta_j\le1\),
\[
v_j(\rho,\theta_j)^2=1-\kappa_j^2(1-\rho)\cos^2\theta_j
\ge1-(1-\rho)=\rho\ge\rho_0>0.
\]
This is solely a statement about the covariance matrix in the limiting Gaussian experiment; no finite-\(n\) covariance is used.

Fix one admissible baseline array \(B\). All limits below are for this array; the theorem does not take a supremum over different arrays.

First consider one stage--\(1\) block, suppress its indices, put \(N=N_{n1s}\), \(m=m_{n1s}\), \(\delta=h_s/\sqrt n\), and write \(G\) for the random complement of the holdout. Hypergeometric variance gives, uniformly for \(\rho\in I\),
\[
\frac{g^1}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2},\qquad
\frac{g^0}{N}\longrightarrow\frac{1-\rho}{2}\quad\text{in probability}.
\]
For \(f_i\) equal to \(B_i-\bar B\), \((B_i-\bar B)^2\), or \((B_i-\bar B)(U_i^0-\bar U^0)\), the without-replacement variance identity and the fourth-moment bound imply
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{i\in G}f_i-\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Nf_i=o_{\mathsf P}(1)
\]
uniformly over all admissible complement sizes. The same conclusion holds after intersecting \(G\) with either treatment arm, because the arm fractions are bounded away from zero with probability tending to one. Hence the random arm variances converge to the full finite-population variance, the selector's exceptional totalization event has probability tending to zero, and
\[
X_{n,s}=A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s+X^0_{n,s}+o_{\mathsf P}(1),
\]
where \(X^0_{n,s}\) is the variance-standardized complement contrast of the fixed \(B\)-values.

The corresponding rank expansion is also explicit. Let \(K_N(\delta)\) be the ordered-pair crossing count. The midrank identity gives
\[
\mathsf E\{\text{treated crossed-pair count}\}
=\frac{m(N-m)}{N(N-1)}K_N(\delta).
\]
Expanding the variance as a sum over two ordered edges, overlapping edge pairs contribute at most a constant times \(NK_N(\delta)\), while disjoint pairs have covariance of order \(N^{-1}\) and contribute at most a constant times \(K_N(\delta)^2/N\). Thus
\[
\operatorname{Var}\{\text{crossed-pair count}\}\le C\{NK_N(\delta)+K_N(\delta)^2/N\}.
\]
The pair-spacing assumption gives \(K_N(\delta)=O(N^{3/2})\), uniformly in \(h\in H\). Since the null rank-sum standard deviation is of order \(N^{3/2}\), the centered crossing term is \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) after studentization, whereas its mean converges to \(b_{1j}h_s\). Moreover, if \(d_i\) is the number of ranks crossed by unit \(i\), then \(\sum_i d_i\le2K_N(\delta)\), \(\max_i d_i\le N\), and
\[
\frac1N\sum_i\left(\frac{d_i}{N}\right)^2\le\frac{2K_N(\delta)}{N^2}=O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Therefore the observed normalized ranks have the same limiting variance and covariance as the baseline midranks. Finiteness of the pair-spacing limit also forces the squared empirical mass of ties to vanish; consequently the normalized-midrank variance tends to \(1/12\). We obtain
\[
R_{1j}=b_{1j}h_s+R^0_{1j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1).
\]
The identical argument in stage \(2\) gives \(R_{2j}=b_{2j}h_s+R^0_{2j}+o_{\mathsf P}(1)\).

Conditional on a representative holdout, \((X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\) is a fixed-dimensional vector of complete-randomization contrasts. The derived maximum-influence bounds apply to every scalar projection. The finite-population vector central limit theorem therefore applies conditionally on such holdouts. The preceding sampling identities show that the exceptional holdouts have probability tending to zero. A direct covariance calculation with the balanced sign \(W_i=2Z_i-1\), using \(\mathsf E(W_iW_l)=-1/(N-1)\) for \(i\ne l\), gives
\[
\operatorname{Corr}(X^0_{n,s},R^0_{1j})\longrightarrow\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}.
\]
Indeed the complement indicator contributes one factor \(1-\rho\) to the covariance and one square-root factor to the selector standard deviation. The stage--\(2\) randomization is independent conditional on the history. Thus, uniformly over the compact parameter domain,
\[
(X_{n,s},R_{1j},R_{2j})\ \Longrightarrow\
\mathcal N\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}A_s\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\\ b_{1j}h_s\\b_{2j}h_s\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}1&\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&0\\
\kappa_j\sqrt{1-\rho}&1&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\right).
\]
Uniformity follows by contradiction: any violating sequence of \((\rho,h,\theta)\) has a convergent subsequence; the uniform moment, share, and pair-spacing premises and the same central limit theorem apply along that subsequence. The residual-scale lemma prevents a singular projected limit.

The same reasoning applies conditionally to the Fisher reference. Under the realized local alternative its fixed completed value is \(B_i+\delta Z_i\). Its empirical second and fourth moments differ from those of \(B\) by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\). Its normalized ranks differ in empirical squared norm by \(o_{\mathsf P}(1)\) by the crossing-degree bound above. Candidate treatment labels are newly completely randomized and hence have zero contrast mean. Candidate holdouts are newly sampled independently, and candidate stage--\(2\) assignments are independent after the candidate cell is retained. It follows, in \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\)-probability and uniformly over \((\rho,h,\theta)\), that the pre-cell reference vector converges to the same Gaussian vector with all three drifts set to zero.

Joint convergence over rectangles and the fixed thresholds gives convergence of the corresponding numerator and cell probabilities. The sampling-selection margin and reference-selection margin bound the relevant denominators below by \(\epsilon\), deterministically eventually for sampling and with probability tending to one for the reference. Applying the conditioning-ratio lemma and the full-cell factorization yields uniform conditional-cdf convergence to \(G_j^h\) and \(G_j^0\), respectively.

It remains to justify the moving critical value. By \(v_j^2\ge\rho_0\), every limiting conditional score has a continuous positive density. Compactness of \(I\), the angle set, the primitive set, and the fixed thresholds bounds all null critical values in one finite interval: Gaussian tail bounds applied before conditioning give finite common lower and upper brackets. On a slightly larger compact interval the conditional density has a positive lower bound. The quantile part of the conditioning-ratio lemma therefore transfers the reference quantiles uniformly.

Let \(a_n=d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\); the preceding argument gives \(a_n\to0\). Let \(Z_n(\rho,h)\) denote the reference distance; for each \(\delta>0\), the argument gives \(\sup_{\rho,h}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{Z_n(\rho,h)>\delta\}\to0\). A diagonal construction chooses \(N_m\uparrow\infty\) so that, for \(n\ge N_m\), \(a_n\le1/m\) and the last supremum at \(\delta=1/m\) is at most \(1/m\); setting \(\eta_n=1/m\) on \([N_m,N_{m+1})\), and enlarging finitely many initial terms, gives \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) with both asserted properties.

Finally, conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\), reference-quantile convergence also holds in probability because the sampling cell probability is at least \(\epsilon\). Decompose the rejection event according as the random critical value lies within \(\zeta\) of \(q_{\alpha,j}\); on the good event, its probability is bracketed by the sampling cdf at \(q_{\alpha,j}\pm\zeta\), and the limiting Gaussian anti-concentration makes the difference vanish as \(\zeta\downarrow0\). The resulting limit is the integral \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\) established by the factorization lemma.

Let \(\gamma_2\) denote standard Gaussian measure on \(\mathbb R^2\), and define
\[
\mathcal O(c,z)=[c,\infty)\times[z,\infty),\qquad
\mathcal T(c,z)=Q^{-1}\{Q(c)Q(z)\}.
\]
Minkowski interpolation of two such orthants is the orthant with interpolated thresholds. The Ehrhard--Borell inequality therefore gives
\[
\mathcal T((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)z_0+tz_1)\le(1-t)\mathcal T(c_0,z_0)+t\mathcal T(c_1,z_1),
\]
because \(Q^{-1}(u)=-\Phi^{-1}(u)\). Thus \(\mathcal T\) is jointly convex. If \(Z\) is standard normal, \(Q(Z)\) is uniform on \((0,1)\), and
\[
\Pr\{\mathcal T(c,Z)>y\}=\frac{Q(y)}{Q(c)},\qquad y>c.
\]
Hence \(\mathcal T(c,Z)\) has the law of a standard normal conditioned to exceed \(c\).

Put \(v=(1-r^2)^{1/2}>0\), \(W(c,z,e)=r\mathcal T(c,z)+ve\), and
\[
\mathcal A(c,q)=\{(z,e):W(c,z,e)\le q\}.
\]
For \(r\ge0\), \(W\) is convex, so
\[
(1-t)\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)+t\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\subseteq
\mathcal A((1-t)c_0+tc_1,(1-t)q_0+tq_1).
\]
Take \(q_i=q_\beta(r,c_i)\). Each set on the left has Gaussian measure \(1-\beta\). Ehrhard--Borell and the inclusion show that the set on the right has measure at least \(1-\beta\). Since \(vE\) gives a strictly positive continuous density, the generalized quantile is unique, and
\[
q_\beta(r,(1-t)c_0+tc_1)\le(1-t)q_\beta(r,c_0)+tq_\beta(r,c_1).
\]
This is convexity.

If \(r=0\), the quantile is the constant \(\Phi^{-1}(1-\beta)\); if \(c_0=c_1\), chord equality is tautological. Conversely, suppose \(r>0\), \(c_0\ne c_1\), and chord equality holds. Then every inequality in the preceding measure comparison is equality. The equality classification for Ehrhard--Borell says that \(\mathcal A(c_0,q_0)\) and \(\mathcal A(c_1,q_1)\) must be parallel half-spaces or equal up to null sets. They are not half-spaces: their boundary is
\[
e=\{q-r\mathcal T(c,z)\}/v,
\]
and \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to c\) as \(z\to-\infty\) but \(\mathcal T(c,z)\to\infty\) as \(z\to\infty\), so this graph is not affine. If the two closed convex sets are equal up to null sets, they are equal, and their boundary graphs give \(\mathcal T(c_0,z)-\mathcal T(c_1,z)\) constant in \(z\). As \(z\to-\infty\), the constant is \(c_0-c_1\). If it were nonzero, the identity \(Q(\mathcal T(c,z))=Q(c)Q(z)\), together with the elementary Mills bounds \(\phi(x)/(x+x^{-1})<Q(x)<\phi(x)/x\) for \(x>0\), would make the ratio \(Q(\mathcal T(c_0,z))/Q(\mathcal T(c_1,z))\) tend to zero or infinity as \(z\to\infty\), whereas it equals the finite positive constant \(Q(c_0)/Q(c_1)\). Thus the constant is zero and then \(c_0=c_1\), a contradiction. The stated equality cases follow.

Fix \(j=(C,s)\), \(\rho\), and \(\theta_j\), and abbreviate \(a=a_j(\rho)>0\), \(d=d_j(\theta_j)>0\), \(r=r_j(\rho,\theta_j)\), and \(q_\alpha=q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)=q_\alpha(r,c_s)\). For \(u\in(\alpha,1)\), the definition of the selected upper quantile gives
\[
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
B_u(h_s):=d h_s+q_u(r,c_s-a h_s)-q_\alpha\ge0.
\]
The selected-quantile theorem makes \(B_u\) convex and continuous. Since \(u>\alpha\), \(B_u(0)=q_u(r,c_s)-q_\alpha(r,c_s)<0\). As \(h_s\to\infty\), the selection threshold tends to \(-\infty\), \(q_u(r,c_s-ah_s)\) tends to the ordinary standard-normal upper-\(u\) quantile, and \(d h_s\to\infty\). Thus \(B_u(h_s)\to\infty\). A continuous convex function negative at zero and tending to infinity has one positive crossing and is nonnegative on the upper interval beginning at that crossing: at a crossing \(x\), its right secant slopes are at least \(\{B_u(x)-B_u(0)\}/x>0\). Therefore the \(u\)-power superlevel set is an upper interval.

Compactness of \(H\) ensures that some \(h\in H\) has coordinate \(h_s=\ell_s\), while every \(h\in H\) has \(h_s\ge\ell_s>0\). The upper-interval property proves
\[
\min_{h\in H}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\ge u
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge u.
\]
Finally, the feasible choice \(\theta_j=\pi/2\) has \(r=0\) and power \(Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_{2j}h_s\}>\alpha\) for every \(h_s>0\). Hence every optimized cell value and the global optimized value are strictly above \(\alpha\). Since all their superlevel predicates above \(\alpha\) coincide under \(H\) and under \(\ell\), their values and their complete argmax sets coincide.

Fix an active pair and suppress its index. Put \(t=\sqrt{1-\rho}\), \(a=At\), \(\gamma=\kappa t\), \(d=b_1\cos\theta+b_2\sin\theta\), \(r=\gamma\cos\theta\), and \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}\). For \(h=\ell_s>0\), write
\[
L=c-ah,\quad K=q_\alpha(r,c)-dh,\quad
u_0=\frac{c-rq_\alpha(r,c)}v,\quad u_h=\frac{L-rK}v,\quad
D_h=\frac{\phi(K)Q(u_h)}{Q(L)}>0.
\]
Let \(\mu(x)=\phi(x)/Q(x)\). Differentiating the bivariate Gaussian upper-tail integral and the null critical equation gives
\[
q_r=\frac{\mu(u_0)}v,\qquad P_d=hD_h,\qquad
P_r=\frac{D_h}{v}\{\mu(u_h)-\mu(u_0)\}.
\]
All divisions are valid because \(v^2\ge\rho_0\), \(Q(L)>0\), and \(D_h>0\). The normal hazard satisfies \(\mu'(x)=\mu(x)\{\mu(x)-x\}\) and \(0<\mu'(x)<1\); the upper bound is the positive-variance identity for a lower-truncated standard normal. Define the secant
\[
\bar s=\frac{\mu(u_0)-\mu(u_h)}{u_0-u_h}\quad\text{if }u_0\ne u_h,\qquad
\bar s=\mu'(u_0)\quad\text{otherwise}.
\]
Then \(0<\bar s<1\) and \(u_0-u_h=h(a-rd)/v\). With \(d'=b_2\cos\theta-b_1\sin\theta\) and \(r'=-\gamma\sin\theta\), the chain rule yields
\[
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}=d'+\frac{\gamma\sin\theta\,(a-rd)\bar s}{v^2}.
\]
The identity \(\cos\theta\,d=b_1+\sin\theta\,d'\) and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1\) give
\[
a-rd=t\Delta-\gamma\sin\theta\,d',\qquad
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}=\mathcal Ld'+\frac{\kappa t^2\sin\theta\,\Delta\bar s}{v^2},\qquad
\mathcal L=1-\frac{\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s}{v^2}>0,
\]
because \(v^2-\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s\ge1-\gamma^2\ge\rho>0\).

Now \(d'\) is positive for \(0\le\theta<\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\), zero at \(\theta_0\), and negative afterward. If \(\Delta>0\), the last display is strictly positive throughout \([0,\theta_0]\), so no maximizer lies there. If \(\Delta<0\), it is strictly negative throughout \([\theta_0,\pi/2]\), while \(P_\theta(0)=hb_2D_h>0\), so every maximizer lies in \((0,\theta_0)\). If \(\Delta=0\), its sign is exactly the sign of \(d'\), proving that \(\theta_0\) is the unique maximizer. Compactness of the angle interval guarantees existence. The least-coordinate theorem shows that these are also the relevant individually optimized weights for the original compact alternative set.

Fix a jointly realizable active stage--\(1\) block and center its baseline values. Write \(\sigma^2\) for their limiting variance and \(\lambda\) for the pair-spacing slope. Convolve the empirical law \(N^{-1}\sum_i\delta_{B_i}\) with the uniform density on an interval of width \(\delta_N=u_\star/\sqrt N\), where \([0,u_\star]\) lies in the declared compact pair-spacing window. If the resulting density is \(f_N\), the ordered-pair convention, including its half weights at ties and endpoints, gives the exact identity
\[
\|f_N\|_2^2=\frac{2}{N^2\delta_N^2}\int_0^{\delta_N}K_N(u)\,du
=\frac{2}{u_\star^2}\int_0^{u_\star}N^{-3/2}K_N(x/\sqrt N)\,dx\longrightarrow\lambda.
\]
The density \(f_N\) has variance \(\sigma_N^2+\delta_N^2/12\), where \(\sigma_N^2\) is the empirical baseline variance with denominator \(N\); the defining limit for \(A\) and the positive share give \(\sigma_N^2\to\sigma^2>0\).

For any centered density \(f\) of variance \(\sigma_f^2>0\), set \(a=\sqrt5\,\sigma_f\) and \(g(x)=3(1-x^2/a^2)_+/(4a)\). Since \((1-x^2/a^2)_+\ge1-x^2/a^2\),
\[
\int fg\ge\frac{3}{4a}\left(1-\frac{\sigma_f^2}{a^2}\right)=\frac{3}{5a},\qquad
\int g^2=\frac{3}{5a}.
\]
The inequality \(\int(f-g)^2\ge0\) therefore gives
\[
\|f\|_2^2\sigma_f\ge\frac{3}{5\sqrt5}.
\]
Apply this inequality to \(f_N\) and pass to the two already established scalar limits. It follows directly that \(\lambda\sigma\ge3/(5\sqrt5)\).
The pair-spacing condition also removes asymptotic atoms, so the normalized midrank has limiting variance \(1/12\). By Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)\le\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{12}}.
\]
Using the definitions \(A=\sqrt{r_1}/(2\sigma)\), \(b_1=\sqrt3\,\lambda\sqrt{r_1}\), and \(\kappa=\sqrt{12}\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)/\sigma\), which are jointly realized by the same array, we obtain
\[
\frac{A\kappa}{b_1}=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(B,U^0)}{\sigma^2\lambda}\le\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}\,\sigma\lambda}\le\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}.
\]
All denominators are positive by the variance, pair-spacing, and primitive-positivity premises.

Fix a cell \(j\) with \(\Delta_j\ge0\) and put \(P(\rho,\theta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\theta,\ell_s)\). In the notation of the weight-side proof, direct differentiation of the upper-tail ratio gives
\[
P_a=h\mu(L)\left[Q\!\left(\frac{q-dh-rL}{v}\right)-P\right]<0\quad(r>0),\qquad
\operatorname{sign}(P_r)=\operatorname{sign}(rd-a).
\]
The first inequality holds because the conditional rejection probability is strictly increasing in the selected \(Z\) when \(r>0\), so its boundary value is below its selected-tail average. Every individually optimal angle satisfies \(\theta\ge\theta_0\). On this interval \(\cos\theta\,d\le b_1\), and hence
\[
a-rd=t\{A-\kappa\cos\theta\,d\}\ge t\Delta\ge0.
\]
Thus \(P_r\le0\). Since \(a_\rho=-A/(2t)\) and \(r_\rho=-\kappa\cos\theta/(2t)\),
\[
P_\rho=-\frac{AP_a+\kappa\cos\theta\,P_r}{2t}>0
\]
for every optimal \(\theta<\pi/2\). The value at \(\theta=\pi/2\) is the constant pure-stage--\(2\) power \(p_2=Q\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2\ell_s\}\).

At the largest holdout, \(t^2=\rho_0\). The inward derivative from \(\theta=\pi/2\) is
\[
\phi\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha)-b_2h\}\left[b_1h-\kappa t\{\mu(c)-\mu(c-Ath)\}\right].
\]
Because \(0<\mu'<1\), the bracket exceeds \(h(b_1-\kappa A t^2)\). The realizability bound and \(\rho_0<1/2\) give
\[
\frac{\kappa A t^2}{b_1}\le\rho_0\frac{5\sqrt{15}}{18}<1,
\]
so pure stage \(2\) is strictly improvable there.

Let \(M_j(\rho)=\max_\theta P(\rho,\theta)\). It is nondecreasing: an optimizer above \(p_2\) is not \(\pi/2\) and its fixed-angle power strictly increases with \(\rho\), while \(p_2\) itself is available everywhere. Its endpoint value is strictly above \(p_2\), so for every smaller \(\rho\), either \(M_j(\rho)=p_2<M_j(1-\rho_0)\), or a maximizing non-pure angle strictly improves by the endpoint. Hence
\[
M_j(\rho)<M_j(1-\rho_0)\qquad(\rho<1-\rho_0).
\]
Taking the finite minimum over \(j\) preserves strict endpoint superiority: choose a cell binding at the endpoint and compare it at the smaller \(\rho\). This proves unique optimality of the holdout fraction. At the endpoint, a binding cell must use an individual maximizing angle; the weight-side theorem and the strict inward derivative place it in \([\theta_{0j},\pi/2)\), with equality exactly for \(\Delta_j=0\). A slack cell need only satisfy \(\Pi_j\ge V^\star\), giving precisely its stated superlevel set.

Before scaling, the stage--\(1\) density equals \(16/5\) on \([-1/10,1/10]\) and \(1/5\) on the remainder of \([-1,1]\). Direct integration gives
\[
\operatorname{Var}(B)=\frac{203}{1500},\qquad
\int f^2=\frac{53}{25},\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\{B,F(B)\}=\frac14\mathsf E|B-B'|=\frac{1393}{15000}.
\]
Scaling by \(L=53\sqrt3/80\) multiplies the variance by \(L^2\), divides the pair slope by \(L\), and multiplies the covariance by \(L\). The stage--\(2\) uniform law has variance \(625/1849\) and pair slope \(43/(50\sqrt3)\). With share \(1/4\), substitution yields
\[
A=\frac{200\sqrt5}{53\sqrt{203}},\qquad b_1=\frac85,\qquad b_2=\frac{43}{100},\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1393\sqrt5}{250\sqrt{203}}.
\]
Exact squaring and rational comparison give the stated outward decimal enclosures and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1<0\).

Both supports are bounded by less than \(1.15\), so every centered empirical fourth moment is eventually below \(2\). Their variances and normalized-rank variances tend to positive constants exceeding \(1/100\); all four shares tend to \(1/4\). For deterministic quantiles of a bounded piecewise-constant density, a uniform Riemann-sum calculation gives
\[
N^{-3/2}K_N(u/\sqrt N)\longrightarrow u\int f^2
\]
uniformly for \(u\) in each fixed compact window. Thus the pair-spacing, moment, share, and variance premises hold. The singleton set of the displayed joint primitive vector is compact and is realized by this one array. No interference, both complete randomizations, the independent simple-random holdout, and fixed thresholds hold by construction.

The split/assignment central limit theorem and the studentizer calculation used in the transfer proof give, uniformly in \(\rho\),
\[
\Pr\{X_{n,s}>-113/100\}\longrightarrow Q\{-113/100-A\sqrt{1-\rho}\,h_s\}\ge Q(-113/100).
\]
The strata are independent, so the both-selected probability has limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\). For the Fisher-completed candidate array, the \(O(n^{-1/2})\) local shifts do not change empirical second moments, and the candidate contrast is null-centered. The same conditional finite-population central limit theorem gives each candidate selection probability converging in sampling probability to \(Q(-113/100)\), uniformly in \((\rho,h)\). Candidate strata are independent, so their product converges to \(Q(-113/100)^2\). Outward-rounded evaluation gives
\[
Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534],
\]
which exceeds \(1/100\). This verifies every member condition of \(\mathcal M\) and both margins.

For this witness both active cells have identical primitives, so their conditional Gaussian powers coincide when their angles coincide. The negative-discrepancy part of the weight-side theorem restricts every endpoint maximizer to \(0<\theta<\theta_0\), where \(\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\).

The numerical inequalities were certified with \(100\)-bit Arb ball arithmetic. For each queried \((\rho,\theta)\), the null critical value was enclosed in an interval of width \(2\cdot10^{-7}\) by checking opposite signs of the defining monotone tail equation. The power integral was evaluated outwardly on \([c-ah,12]\), and the omitted remainder was bounded by \(Q(12)<10^{-31}\). At the rational interior point, the resulting enclosure was
\[
\Pi_j(5034/10000,25363/100000,33/20)\in
[0.8642862126664672633,\ 0.8642862583791498921].
\]

To cover an entire endpoint angle continuum, differentiating the Gaussian integral gives on \(0\le\theta\le\theta_0\)
\[
|\partial_\theta\Pi_j|\le
\frac{h}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,Q(c-ah)}\left[b_2+\frac{\gamma\sin\theta_0\{a+\gamma\sqrt{b_1^2+b_2^2}\}}{1-\gamma^2}\right]=:L_\theta.
\]
All denominators are positive because \(\gamma^2\le1-\rho_0<1\). A \(129\)-point uniform mesh, enlarged by \(L_\theta\theta_0/256\), certified
\[
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.02,\theta,33/20)\le0.8630457385441023483,\qquad
\sup_{\theta\in[0,\pi/2]}\Pi_j(0.98,\theta,33/20)\le0.8624116251942651582.
\]
The restriction from the weight-side theorem covers the complement of the meshed interval. These upper bounds are strictly below \(0.86304573855\) and \(0.86241162520\), while the interior lower bound is strictly above \(0.86428621266\). The transfer theorem identifies these Gaussian quantities as the limiting rejection powers using the separate shifted sampling law and zero-drift Fisher critical law. Hence neither endpoint can maximize the limiting worst-cell objective; compactness guarantees an optimizer, and every maximizing holdout fraction is strictly interior.

The residual-scale bound places \(|r_j|\) uniformly below one. The bivariate Gaussian upper tail is real analytic in its two thresholds and correlation on this compact positive-definite domain. Its derivative with respect to the critical threshold is a strictly negative Gaussian density. The analytic implicit-function theorem therefore makes \(q_{\alpha,j}\), and hence \(p_j(\rho,\theta)=\Pi_j(\rho,\theta,\ell_s)\), real analytic on a neighborhood of \(I\times[0,\pi/2]\).

Let \(A_j=\partial_\theta p_j\). The derivative formula in the weight-side proof gives \(A_j(\rho,0)=b_{2j}\ell_sD_{\ell_s}>0\), so \(A_j\) is not identically zero on any two-dimensional open set. Its zero set on the compact rectangle is semianalytic of dimension at most one. The finite semianalytic-stratification theorem decomposes it into finitely many analytic arcs and points. Splitting arcs at critical values of projection onto \(\rho\), at multiple roots, and at the rectangle boundary produces finitely many graphs \(\theta_{j\ell}(\rho)\) on open subintervals. At their endpoints the local Weierstrass polynomial gives the stated finite Puiseux continuation; persistent repeated factors are reduced and retained rather than discarded.

For a fixed \(\rho\), a maximum in \(\theta\) occurs at an angular endpoint or at one of these stationary graphs. Consequently
\[
M_j(\rho)=\max_\ell g_{j\ell}(\rho),\qquad
g_{j\ell}(\rho)=p_j\{\rho,\theta_{j\ell}(\rho)\},\qquad
F(\rho)=\min_jM_j(\rho),
\]
with angular endpoints included as branches. Refine the finite interval decomposition at all nonidentical branch crossings, nontransverse crossings, and projected arc endpoints. On every remaining interval the ordering of all branches and cells is fixed, so \(F\) equals one analytic branch. Such a branch attains an interior maximum only at a stationary root unless it is constant; a constant branch contributes its entire flat interval. Adding both endpoints of \(I\), all projected branch endpoints, all stationary roots, all branch intersections, and all flat intervals is therefore exhaustive and necessary. Multiple-root, tie, and identical-branch predicates are exactly those retained by the branch system, so no genericity or exact numerical equality decision has been imposed. The argument is independent of the signs of the \(\Delta_j\); the weight-side and endpoint theorems merely prune candidates on their respective strata.

It remains to recover all weights. Independence of the cell-specific angles gives, for fixed \(\rho\),
\[
\max_{(\theta_j)}\min_jp_j(\rho,\theta_j)=\min_j\max_{\theta_j}p_j(\rho,\theta_j)=F(\rho).
\]
The first inequality in each direction follows respectively by choosing every cellwise maximizer and by bounding each \(p_j\) by \(M_j\). Thus a design attains \(V^\star\) if and only if its holdout is in the exhaustive maximizing set just described and every coordinate satisfies \(p_j(\rho,\theta_j)\ge V^\star\). This is precisely the displayed product of full superlevel sets, including all slack-cell continua, and proves necessity and sufficiency.

For algebraic or rational inputs, \(\phi\), \(\Phi\), and their derivatives have terminating outward rational enclosures on compact intervals by their power series together with standard Gaussian tail bounds. The residual-scale lemma supplies \(v\ge\sqrt{\rho_0}>0\). Choose a finite rational \(M\) so that the unconditional Gaussian tails outside \([-M,M]\) are smaller than the fixed conditional-tail margins. Then every null critical value lies in \([-M,M]\). On this compact set the derivative of the defining tail probability with respect to \(q\) is a continuous strictly negative Gaussian density and hence has an effectively positive lower enclosure. Bisection with outward tail integration therefore terminates for every requested critical-value accuracy. Differentiating the integral on the enlarged compact domain supplies an effective common oscillation bound for every \(\Pi_j\), and hence for the finite minimum objective
\[
\Psi(\rho,\theta)=\min_{j\in J}\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s).
\]

Fix rational \(\varepsilon>0\). Subdivide the compact design domain into finitely many rational boxes until interval evaluation supplies an enclosure \([L_B,U_B]\) of \(\Psi\) on every box with \(U_B-L_B\le\delta\), where \(0<\delta\le\varepsilon\). Set \(L^\star=\max_B L_B\) and \(U^\star=\max_B U_B\). A box containing an optimizer shows \(L^\star\le V^\star\le U^\star\), and \(U_B\le L_B+\delta\le L^\star+\delta\) for every \(B\), so \(U^\star-L^\star\le\delta\le\varepsilon\).

Retain in the outer union every box with \(U_B\ge L^\star\). Every optimizer box is retained. For any retained box and every point in it,
\[
\Psi\ge L_B\ge U_B-\delta\ge L^\star-\delta\ge V^\star-2\delta\ge V^\star-2\varepsilon.
\]
Thus the outer union is contained in the \(2\varepsilon\)-power superlevel set. Any boxes satisfying \(L_B\ge U^\star-\varepsilon\) form a finite inner union, possibly empty, on which \(\Psi\ge V^\star-\varepsilon\). Every comparison is between rational interval endpoints, so equality of arbitrary exact reals is never queried.

Finally, a supplied separation certificate is checked by interval root existence and uniqueness on its isolating boxes, exclusion bounds on their complements, strict interval comparisons of all competing branch values, and a positive objective gap outside the winning neighborhoods. If all checks pass, the branch characterization excludes every other optimizer and refinement yields arbitrarily small boxes around the unique design. Without those checks, the algorithm reports only the value and set enclosures just proved and makes no uniqueness assertion.

When every \(\Delta_j=0\), the weight-side theorem says that the unique individual maximizer is \(\theta_{0j}=\arctan(b_{2j}/b_{1j})\). Identical primitives make the two conditional-power functions, and therefore their envelopes, identical. The global-endpoint theorem gives the unique holdout fraction \(1-\rho_0\). Since both cells bind and each has a unique individual weight, the stated proportional design follows.

theorem.statement: The frozen class does not determine a sharp necessary-and-sufficient shrinking-margin frontier solely from \(m_n\) and the sequence \(\eta_n(B)\). For any joint numerator-and-denominator approximation with absolute error at most \(\eta_n(B)\) and limiting cell probability at least \(m_n>\eta_n(B)\), conditional-cdf error is at most \(2\eta_n(B)/(m_n-\eta_n(B))\); hence \(\eta_n(B)=o(m_n)\) is a universal sufficient relation. It is not necessary as a relation involving the declared \(\eta_n(B)\), because that sequence is a noncanonical upper bound that may be enlarged without changing any law or conditional error. Moreover, the frozen sampling and reference margin assumptions impose a fixed positive \(\epsilon\), so no \(m_n\downarrow0\) regime occurs inside \(\mathcal M\). A sharp failure sequence therefore requires an enlarged class together with a canonical minimal joint-approximation modulus and explicit moving-threshold or boundary-density conditions; it cannot be constructed or characterized from the frozen primitives alone.
theorem.proof_tex:
Apply the conditioning-ratio lemma with \(\delta=\eta_n(B)\) and \(m=m_n\). It gives the displayed cdf bound, which tends to zero whenever \(\eta_n(B)/m_n\to0\). If the limiting selected cdf has density lower bound \(g_n\) near its critical quantile, the same lemma gives quantile error at most \(2\eta_n(B)/\{g_n(m_n-\eta_n(B))\}\); local-power transfer follows by the same threshold bracketing and anti-concentration. Thus the sufficient condition must also track \(g_n\) when residual or boundary densities are allowed to degenerate.

Necessity cannot be inferred from the named remainder. The transfer theorem asserts only existence of one deterministic upper sequence: if \(\eta_n(B)\) works, then every decreasing \(\widetilde\eta_n(B)\ge\eta_n(B)\) with \(\widetilde\eta_n(B)\to0\) also works. For example, after truncating at one, \(\widetilde\eta_n=\sqrt{\eta_n}\) is another valid declared remainder. The truth of conditional convergence is unchanged, but the ratios to a chosen \(m_n\) can have different limits. More fundamentally, an absolute joint error bound does not specify whether numerator and denominator errors cancel in their ratio, so it cannot yield a necessary condition.

Finally, \(\mathrm{ass{:}sampling\mbox{-}selection\mbox{-}margin}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}reference\mbox{-}selection\mbox{-}margin}\) bound all represented cell probabilities below by the fixed number \(\epsilon>0\), eventually or with probability tending to one. Hence a sequence \(m_n\downarrow0\) is outside the frozen population class. Producing the requested below-frontier finite-population witness would necessarily alter fixed thresholds or the margin assumptions and would require a canonical error modulus plus lower-bound geometry not present in the core. The negative characterization in the statement is therefore the maximal conclusion determined by the supplied handle.

added_lemmas.statement: Consider a sequence of finite populations of fixed-dimensional vectors assigned by complete randomization to a fixed number of groups whose limiting proportions are positive. If every scalar projection satisfies the finite-population maximum-influence condition and the correlation matrices converge, then the coordinatewise variance-standardized vector of group-contrast estimators converges in distribution to the centered Gaussian vector having the limiting correlation matrix.

attestation.note: Checked against the primary arXiv PDF; the stable handles are supplied in place of a verbatim transcription.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P_n\) and \(P\) be probability laws, let \(E_n,E\) be events, and let \(A_n(x)\subseteq E_n\) and \(A(x)\subseteq E\) be nested events indexed by \(x\in\mathbb R\). If \(P(E)\ge m>\delta\), \(\lvert P_n(E_n)-P(E)\rvert\le\delta\), and \(\sup_x\lvert P_n(A_n(x))-P(A(x))\rvert\le\delta\), then
\[
\sup_x\left\lvert P_n\{A_n(x)\mid E_n\}-P\{A(x)\mid E\}\right\rvert\le \frac{2\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
If the conditional limit cdf has density at least \(g>0\) on a radius-\(a\) neighborhood of its \(p\)-quantile and the left side is at most \(e<ag\), then the generalized \(p\)-quantile differs from the limiting quantile by at most \(e/g\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(p_n=P_n(E_n)\), \(p=P(E)\), \(a_n(x)=P_n(A_n(x))\), and \(a(x)=P(A(x))\). The assumptions give \(p_n\ge m-\delta>0\), while \(0\le a(x)\le p\). Therefore
\[
\left|\frac{a_n(x)}{p_n}-\frac{a(x)}p\right|\le
\frac{|a_n(x)-a(x)|}{p_n}+\frac{a(x)|p_n-p|}{p_np}\le
\frac{\delta}{m-\delta}+\frac{\delta}{m-\delta}.
\]
Taking the supremum proves the first assertion. For the second, write \(q\) for the limiting \(p\)-quantile and \(F_n,F\) for the conditional cdfs. If \(0<t<a\), the density bound implies \(F(q-t)\le p-gt\) and \(F(q+t)\ge p+gt\). When \(t>e/g\), uniform cdf error gives \(F_n(q-t)<p\) and \(F_n(q+t)>p\). The definition \(q_n=\inf\{x:F_n(x)\ge p\}\) then yields \(q-t<q_n\le q+t\). Letting \(t\downarrow e/g\) proves \(|q_n-q|\le e/g\).

added_lemmas.statement:
For closed convex sets \(A_0,A_1\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) and \(0<t<1\), Gaussian measure satisfies the Ehrhard--Borell inequality
\[
\Phi^{-1}\!\bigl(\gamma_d((1-t)A_0+tA_1)\bigr)\ge(1-t)\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_d(A_0))+t\Phi^{-1}(\gamma_d(A_1)).
\]
When both measures lie strictly between zero and one, equality for weights summing to one occurs only when the sets are parallel half-spaces or when \(A_0=A_1\), apart from Gaussian-null modifications.

attestation.note: Checked against the primary arXiv PDF; the node records only the convex-set inequality and the weights-summing-to-one equality alternatives used in the proof.

added_lemmas.statement: A finite family of real-analytic functions admits, locally, Weierstrass polynomial preparation and a compatible semianalytic stratification. A relatively compact semianalytic set consequently has finitely many connected components and a finite compatible stratification into connected real-analytic manifolds. In dimension one, every punctured local branch is the image of a real-analytic, equivalently finitely ramified Puiseux, arc; projections of relatively compact subanalytic sets are subanalytic and have locally finite fibers and components. At a simple zero, the corresponding branch is an analytic graph by the analytic implicit-function theorem.

proposed.statement: For every fixed admissible baseline array \(B=(B_n)_n\), there is an array-dependent deterministic sequence \(\eta_n(B)\downarrow0\) with two separate conclusions. First, the sampling distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\), formed from the family of separately indexed laws \(\{\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}:\rho\in I,h\in H\}\), satisfies \(d_n^{\mathrm{samp}}(B)\le\eta_n(B)\); hence the sampling cdf conditional on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\) converges to \(G_j^h(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) uniformly over \(\rho\in I\), \(\theta\in[0,\pi/2]^J\), and \(h\in H\). Second, each \(\rho\)-indexed dataset \(\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho}\sim\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) generates its own completion, kernel, cdf \(F^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), critical value \(q^{\mathrm{ref}}_{n,j}(\rho,\theta_j,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and distance \(d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})\), and \(\sup_{\rho\in I,\,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{d_n^{\mathrm{ref}}(B,\rho,\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho})>\eta_n(B)\}\to0\). Thus the random Fisher-reference cdf and critical value converge in their corresponding sampling probabilities to \(G_j^0(\cdot;\rho,\theta_j)\) and \(q_{\alpha,j}(\rho,\theta_j)\), uniformly in the displayed outer supremum. The permutation approximation uses the maximum-influence bounds derived in \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}max\mbox{-}influence}\), while selected Gaussian ratio and anti-concentration bounds use the common lower margin \(\min\{\epsilon,\rho_0\}\) from the selection or variance premises and \(\mathrm{lem{:}derived\mbox{-}residual\mbox{-}scale}\). After \(\mathrm{lem{:}full\mbox{-}cell\mbox{-}factorization}\), the rejection probability under each \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) converges uniformly to \(\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,h_s)\). No deterministic rate is asserted uniformly over all baseline arrays in \(\mathcal M\), and no finite-\(n\) covariance bound is inferred from the limiting \(\rho_0\) inequality.
proposed.justification: This is the load-bearing bridge from exact full-cell finite-population conditioning to the scalar Gaussian design criterion.
proposed.gap: Li--Ding and Shi--Ding control unconditional randomization statistics, while Tian--Taylor transfers iid laws through smooth randomized selection; none handles the complete signed cell, coupled without-replacement selector, random complement counts, studentization, imputed null reference, and moving selected quantile with one remainder.
proposed.consumer: It turns analytic Gaussian holdout choices into uniformly valid asymptotic full-cell conditional-power statements for finite randomized enrichment trials.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the finite-population central limit theorem and the proved conditioning-ratio lemma used by the transfer proof.

proposed.statement: For every \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0\le r<1\), the map \(x\mapsto q_{\beta}(r,x)\) is convex on \(\mathbb R\). Moreover, for every \(c_0,c_1\in\mathbb R\) and \(0<t<1\), \(\operatorname{Eq}_{\beta,r}(c_0,c_1;t)\) holds if and only if \(r=0\) or \(c_0=c_1\).
proposed.justification: Convexity supplies the global single-crossing fact needed to optimize over arbitrary compact alternatives.
proposed.gap: Shenfeld and van Handel prove Gaussian-measure convexity and equality cases but do not derive convexity of conditional selected-score quantiles.
proposed.consumer: Power calculations need only the least clinically relevant effect coordinate, even when the prespecified alternative set is nonconvex.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the Ehrhard--Borell inequality and equality classification used to derive convexity and strict chord equality.

proposed.statement: With \(M_4=2\) and \(\epsilon=1/100\), the baseline triangular array \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\), and \(\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\) is its chronological local-alternative law. Its bounded symmetric supports give the empirical centered fourth-moment inequality in \(\mathrm{ass{:}bounded\mbox{-}fourth\mbox{-}moments}\). Substitution of its deterministic quantiles into the exact formulas for \(X\), \(R_1\), and \(R_2\) gives, for both active pairs \(j=((1,1),s)\), \(A_s=200\sqrt5/(53\sqrt{203})\), \(b_{1j}=8/5\), \(b_{2j}=43/100\), and \(\kappa_j=1393\sqrt5/(250\sqrt{203})\), with the certified enclosures in \(\mathrm{def{:}negative\mbox{-}mixture\mbox{-}witness}\) and \(\Delta_j\in[-0.80693126929013,-0.80693126929009]\). Uniformly over \(\rho\in I\) and \(h\in H\), the sampling probability of \(E_{n,(1,1)}(\rho)\) has limit inferior at least \(Q(-113/100)^2\in[0.75822626517532,0.75822626517534]\). Moreover, for every \(\delta>0\), \(\sup_{\rho\in I,h\in H}\mathsf P_n^{h,\rho}\{\lvert p_{\mathrm{ref}}(n,(1,1),\mathcal D_n^{h,\rho},\rho)-Q(-113/100)^2\rvert>\delta\}\to0\). Thus \(W_{\mathrm{mix}}\) satisfies both the deterministic sampling margin and the random-reference margin.
proposed.justification: This verifies joint finite-population realizability and exposes every numerical ingredient used by the interior certificate.
proposed.gap: Gaussian-coordinate counterexamples alone need not correspond to any randomized finite population; this proposition realizes the signed regime with exact bounded distributions and certified primitive boxes.
proposed.consumer: A referee can reproduce the negative-discrepancy example from its mixture weights, supports, allocation, and exact radical primitives.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the finite-population central limit theorem used to verify the witness's sampling and random-reference margins.

proposed.statement: On every primitive stratum defined by \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\mbox{-}system}\), each active cell's complete-event conditional envelope \(M_j\) and the global envelope \(F\) are finite maxima and minima of analytic or Puiseux-continuable branches. The global maximizing holdout set consists exactly of the retained interval endpoints, projected branch endpoints, stationary branch roots, branch intersections, and flat maximizing intervals attaining \(V^{\star}\); for each such \(\rho\), the full weight set is \(\prod_{j=(C,s)\in J}\{\theta_j:\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\ge V^{\star}\}\). This characterization is necessary and sufficient in all positive, negative, zero, and mixed-sign \(\Delta\) regimes, with every \(\Pi_j\) conditioned on \(E_{n,C}(\rho)\).
proposed.justification: This supplies the complete mixed-sign analytic geometry and preserves all ties and slack-cell weight continua.
proposed.gap: Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu optimize a discretized policy program and do not characterize the continuous holdout argmax correspondence or its equality strata.
proposed.consumer: The complete candidate list supports auditable global design optimization even when the optimizer is nonunique or lies on a branch transition.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Declare the classical finite semianalytic-stratification result that makes the branch list exhaustive.
